findings.reason: it removes a whole function and a branch instead of rewiring them, shrinking the §8 node and eliminating the fifth copy outright rather than converting it to a shim.
findings.text: §8 lists client.py's `_slurm_service_uri` (and the SLURM branch of `_resolve_graph_uri`, client.py:145-151) as a fifth live copy and proposes to make it *delegate* its SLURM discovery to `resolve_service_url`, keeping the function. But `profiles.py`'s Mode 2 already runs `discover_compute_node_local(...)` on a compute node with no `local` gate (profiles.py:313, with the comment "Discovery decides reachability here, not the hostname"), and `_resolve_graph_uri` already obtains the profile URI through `get_graph_uri()` before overriding it. So on a compute node `get_graph_uri()` already returns `bolt://<service-node>:<port>` — the same value `_slurm_service_uri` builds — and the override wrapper is redundant today; its docstring ("the profile layer does not recognise a compute node as local") describes the pre-repair state that profiles.py has already fixed. The honest change is to delete `_slurm_service_uri` and the SLURM override in `_resolve_graph_uri` once `resolve_service_url` is the owner, rather than retain a delegating wrapper whose only job is to reproduce what `get_graph_uri()` returns.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the two structural sections are consolidations into one owner, not a spread of wrappers: §8 makes a single `resolve_service_url` the SLURM-discovery owner that five call sites delegate to; §9 collapses one remote probe and one DataAccess writer into `ingest_discovered_signals`. No section hides the same behaviour behind several shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §8 keeps `_slurm_service_uri` in `imas_codex/graph/client.py` and the SLURM branch of `_resolve_graph_uri` as delegating copies, but `profiles.py`'s Mode 2 already resolves a compute node (`if info.scheduler == "slurm":` is unconditional on `local`, `imas_codex/graph/profiles.py:313`), so the graph path already resolves correctly without them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts this week are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. Every section that touches a family accounts in its own text: §2 names its three FacilitySignal slots and the `SignalDataClass` enum and names the retired `class:`/`shots:`/`udpid:` keyword parking; §3 names `fronts_database` and states why nothing can be retired (no existing WikiPage property records the database a rendered page fronts); §8 states no public definition is added and two private copies plus one rewrite are removed; §9 adds no public surface. No section adds a CLI option or an MCP view.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and extends existing machinery at every point: the EDAS scanner (`imas_codex/discovery/signals/scanners/edas.py`) rather than a sibling scanner, `link_chunks_to_entities` + the existing `WikiChunk-[:DOCUMENTS]->FacilitySignal` edge and the `WikiPageStatus` enum rather than a new `DOCUMENTED_IN` edge or a widened enum (§3), `resolve_service_url`/`discover_compute_node_local` as the SLURM owner (§8), `probe_remote_environment` and `ingest_discovered_signals` (§9). The updated decision text and the §3 review comment record that a new-edge proposal was withdrawn in favour of the existing relationship.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the wrapper the plan retains, `get_embed_host`/`_embed_host_from_facility` in `imas_codex/settings.py`, is a host-shaped accessor with at least six consumers (`cli/services.py`, `cli/embed.py`, `cli/compute.py` (three call sites), `discovery/base/services.py`, `embeddings/readiness.py`); the plan justifies keeping it (the owner constructs URLs, a host-shaped need is served from the URL) and removes its private discovery copy. That is an adapter over the owner with a stated reason, not a parallel mechanism.
